summary: AppLocker allowlist still allows Windows management tools that can stop or weaken Guard
evidence: The generated policy uses New-AppLockerPolicy -AllowWindows and only adds explicit deny rules for Taskmgr.exe. Standard Windows tools such as taskkill.exe/cmd.exe/powershell.exe can remain allowed by default Windows rules.
fix_plan: Add a deny list for process/system management tools when child-side management tools are blocked, and make runtime stop those processes too.

summary: Blocked Windows management tool bypasses in AppControl mode
evidence: Added management-tool deny paths for AppLocker and runtime blocking for taskmgr/taskkill/cmd/PowerShell/reg/mmc/schtasks/sc/net/script hosts.

summary: Existing AppControl installs would not automatically receive the stronger policy
evidence: Policy application was gated only by PolicyUpdatePending, so an existing Enforced/Audit state with pending=false could keep the old AppLocker XML until a parent changed settings.
fix_plan: Added PolicySchemaVersion and NeedsApply so old active policies are reapplied once.
verify_command: Guard.Tests.exe detects stale application control policy schema
